newsitem.title: FRANCE: AOL has 25,000 subscribers in France.
newsitem.headline: AOL has 25,000 subscribers in France.

text.p: Online service group AOL said on Wednesday it had signed up 25,000 subscribers in France and would soon hit the 30,000 mark.
A spokeswoman for AOL, a joint venture between Bertelsmann AG and America Online, said the firm was pleased with the growth rate in France which was higher than the market average.
"The significant number of subscribers that have joined us in so little time reflects the performance of our service," Bertrand Le Ficher, managing director of AOL France, said.
AOL started its service in France in March. CompuServe, which has been active in France for a number of years, had 70,000 subscribers in France at the start of December.
Wanadoo, the online service of France Telecom which started in April, has 13,000 subscribers.
AOL France has just launched version 3.0 of its software, which offers improved mail facilities and has an integrated Microsoft Explorer browers for easier surfing on the Internet.
America Online is the biggest online service provider in the world with over seven million subscribers, the overwhelming majority of them in the United States
In Europe, AOL has been operating in France, German and Britain since last year and has 300,000 subscribers.

"The initial subscriber numbers are much more than we expected. Due to this success, AOL is continuing its expansion and will start this week in Switzerland and in Austria and will do so in Sweden in early 1997," the company said.
AOL has partnerships with a large number of content providers including the national services of Reuters Holdings Plc for real-time news.

At the start of French service, Le Ficher said he aimed for 500,000 subscribers in four years and Thomas Middelhoff, board member at Bertelsmann, said he aimed to overtake CompuServe in Europe within two years.
